```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
site_url <- "https://insightsurge.github.io/mascot/"
library(mascot) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
```

## In a minute

`mascot` puts a small character drawn in code into your Shiny app or Quarto page. It shows a mood with a status line beside it, and wiggles into the new face when the mood changes. You control it from R with plain arguments, with no AI service involved. It is built for good-practice (`GxP`) work, sitting beside your ordinary field errors and results rather than replacing them.

What you get:

- **A character with moods:** four built-in characters with five shared moods (`"idle"`, `"thinking"`, `"happy"`, `"worried"` and `"celebrating"`).
- **Status text beside it:** a visible text line next to the drawing so the face never speaks alone.
- **Smooth motion:** a short wiggle on mood changes, plus nods and waves that respect reduced-motion settings.
- **Light and dark mode:** follows your `bslib` colour toggle or Quarto's theme mode.
- **Your colours:** built-in palettes, custom light and dark colours, or brand colours from `bslib::bs_theme()`.
- **Offline by design:** ships every script and style in the package, and shows a worried face if Shiny disconnects.
- **A studio to explore:** [`mascot_studio()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_studio.html")`) (experimental) lets you try every function live and copy the R code.

Install the development version of `mascot` from GitHub with `pak`:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("insightsurge/mascot")
```

## Try it without writing code

The fastest way to see what `mascot` can do is the studio, a small app that runs on your computer and needs no internet. It is experimental, so its looks may change, and it uses the optional `bslib` and `knitr` packages.

- [`mascot_studio()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_studio.html")`) opens the studio. Pick a character, pick a function from the list, change its arguments and watch the mascot react. The R code to copy sits under the picture and always matches what you see.
- Each function has a short guide page in the studio, with the same text as the website's guide pages (**Guides** menu, **Studio guide: every function**).
- `mascot_studio(view = "theme")` (or `mascot_example("theme")`) opens **Theme a mascot**. Choose one character, then try a ready-made palette, your own colours for light and dark mode, or the colours of your app's `bslib` theme. Its **Check** tab shows every mood in light and dark and warns about low contrast, and the code to copy is the shortest `mascot_theme()` call that gives the same look.
- `mascot_studio(view = "examples")` lists the bundled example apps. You can also open the theme page from the studio's **More** menu.
- To start on one function or character, name them: `mascot_studio(fn = "mascot_theme", character = "sela")`.

```{r studio-start, eval=FALSE}
mascot_studio()
mascot_studio(view = "theme")
```

## Your first app

Suppose you have a batch review page where Tessa, the default character, waits in the corner until someone clicks **Finish review**, then smiles and confirms that every row passed. Put this code in an `app.R` file and run it from an interactive R session:

```{r first-app, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(mascot)

ui <- fluidPage(
  h1("Batch review"),
  actionButton("finish", "Finish review"),
  mascot("helper", status = "Ready to review")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$finish, {
    update_mascot(
      "helper",
      mood = "happy",
      status = "Review complete",
      bubble = mascot_bubble("All rows checked.", duration = 5)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

How each line works:

- `library(shiny)` and `library(mascot)` load Shiny and the package.
- [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) adds Tessa in the bottom-right corner with the id `"helper"` and `"Ready to review"` beside her.
- `observeEvent(input$finish, { ... })` waits for your user to click **Finish review**.
- [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) updates `"helper"` in place using the same id.
- `mood = "happy"` and `status = "Review complete"` change Tessa's face and status text together.
- [`mascot_bubble()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_bubble.html")`) shows a speech bubble above Tessa that closes after five seconds (`duration = 5`).

## Open an example

You can try the bundled Shiny apps before writing your own code.

- [`mascot_examples()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_examples.html")`) lists the seven bundled example apps in teaching order.
- [`mascot_example()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_example.html")`) runs an example by name, or returns the path to its `app.R` with `run = FALSE`.
- [`mascot_studio()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_studio.html")`) (experimental) opens an interactive playground where you can click through every function and copy the code.

```{r open-example-list}
mascot_examples()
```

```{r open-example-run, eval=FALSE}
mascot_example("form-check")
mascot_studio()
```

## The big ideas

- **One id connects UI and server:** pass the same id string to [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) in the UI and [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) in the server, naming all other arguments.
- **Mood plus status text:** the text beside the character carries the meaning for your users and screen readers, so the face never stands alone.
- **`NULL` leaves a setting unchanged:** in `update_mascot()`, `NULL` keeps the current value on the page, while an empty helper resets it.
- **Bad runtime values warn without crashing:** invalid values in `update_mascot()` warn and leave the mascot untouched instead of stopping the app.
- **Helpers are optional shortcuts:** pass a plain value like `size = 180`, or use [`mascot_size()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_size.html")`) when you want extra options.

## Moods and status

When a form has missing entries or a report takes 20 seconds to build, update the mood and status line together so people using your app can see what is happening.

- Every character has five shared moods (`"idle"`, `"thinking"`, `"happy"`, `"worried"` and `"celebrating"`), listed by [`mascot_moods()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_moods.html")`).
- Set a mood by name or with [`mascot_mood()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_mood.html")`) in [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) and [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`).
- Leave `status = NULL` in `mascot()` to use the mood's default status line, or pass your own text with [`mascot_status()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_status.html")`).
- For a slow task, show the `"thinking"` mood first, do the work, then update the mood when it finishes (`"long-task"` in [`mascot_example()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_example.html")`) shows how).
- Choose a character with [`mascot_character()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_character.html")`), list them with [`mascot_characters()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_characters.html")`), and see their families and attachment points with [`mascot_families()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_families.html")`) and [`mascot_anchors()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_anchors.html")`).
- Tessa and Sela are stable, while Knurl and Neer are experimental and may change (with a warning one release before any removal).

```{r moods-and-characters}
mascot_characters()
mascot_moods("tessa")
```

```{r mood-status-update, eval=FALSE}
update_mascot("helper", mood = "worried", status = "2 fields need attention")
update_mascot("helper", mood = "happy", status = mascot_status())
```

You can read and check a character file with [`mascot_read_character()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_read_character.html")`) or [`mascot_check_character()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_check_character.html")`) (both experimental) and pass the result to `mascot_character()`, `mascot()`, `update_mascot()` or [`mascot_preview()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_preview.html")`). Saving and registering characters and palettes are planned for a later release. See [Write your own character](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/write-your-own-character.html")`) for details.

## Message bubbles

While the status line shows the current state, a speech bubble announces a specific event, such as three skipped rows in an uploaded file.

- Pass a string or [`mascot_bubble()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_bubble.html")`) to `bubble` in [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) or [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`).
- A bubble stays for five seconds (`duration = 5`) and shows a close button by default.
- Use `duration = Inf` for a message your user must act on so it stays until closed or cleared with `mascot_bubble()`.
- The timer pauses on hover, on keyboard focus, or while the mascot is minimised.
- Bubbles stay open across mood changes and character swaps.
- Plain text is escaped, or you can pass trusted markup with `htmltools::HTML()` or self-contained `htmltools` tags.

```{r bubbles-helpers, results="hide"}
mascot_bubble("Three rows skipped.")
mascot_bubble("Check the dates in column B.", duration = Inf)
mascot_bubble()
```

```{r bubbles-update, eval=FALSE}
update_mascot(
  "helper",
  mood = "worried",
  status = "Import needs attention",
  bubble = mascot_bubble("Check the dates in column B.", duration = Inf)
)
```

## One-off gestures

When someone saves a filter or switches tabs, a one-off gesture plays a quick nod or wave without changing the character's mood.

- Send a gesture from the server with `gesture` in [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`), using a name like `"nod"` or [`mascot_gesture()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_gesture.html")`).
- Every character has `"nod"` to acknowledge an action and `"wave"` to greet, listed by [`mascot_gestures()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_gestures.html")`).
- If you change the mood and send a gesture in the same call, the new mood appears first.
- A character swap already includes a greeting wave, so any extra gesture in that update is skipped.
- Reduced-motion settings or [`mascot_motion_settings()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_motion_settings.html")`) can skip the movement while keeping the rest of the update.

```{r gestures-listing}
mascot_gestures("tessa")
```

```{r gesture-update, eval=FALSE}
update_mascot("helper", gesture = mascot_gesture("nod"))
```

## Size and placement

A mascot can float in a window corner as an app-wide helper or sit inline inside a card right next to a form.

- By default, [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) draws at `160` pixels in the `"bottom-right"` corner with a minimise button (`minimise = TRUE`).
- Set `size` to a pixel number (at least `24`), a percentage like `"20%"`, or [`mascot_size()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_size.html")`).
- On phone screens, `small_screen = "auto"` shrinks floating mascots to at most `96` pixels while leaving inline mascots unchanged.
- Set `placement` to `"inline"`, a corner name like `"top-left"`, or [`mascot_placement()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_placement.html")`).
- Minimising a floating mascot turns it into a round restore button and sets `input$<id>_minimised` in Shiny.
- Set `drag = "snap"` for corner snapping or `drag = "free"` (experimental) for free dragging, which updates `input$<id>_position` in Shiny.

```{r size-placement-helpers, results="hide"}
mascot_size(180, small_screen = 72)
mascot_placement("bottom-right", minimise = TRUE, drag = "snap")
```

```{r size-placement-app, eval=FALSE}
mascot("card_helper", size = 120, placement = "inline")
mascot("corner_helper", placement = mascot_placement("bottom-right", drag = "snap"))
update_mascot("corner_helper", placement = mascot_placement("top-left"))
```

## Theme and light/dark mode

When your app has its own brand palette or a dark mode switch, you can match the character's colours through `theme`.

- Leave `theme = NULL` in [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) to keep the character's own colours (or pass `"original"` in [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) to restore them).
- Pick a built-in palette from [`mascot_palettes()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_palettes.html")`), such as `theme = "coral_navy"` for Tessa.
- Use [`mascot_colour_roles()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_colour_roles.html")`) to see a character's parts and which leader roles they follow when you set only a few colours.
- Pass `light` and `dark` lists in [`mascot_theme()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_theme.html")`) for separate light and dark colours, or `css` for browser CSS variables (experimental).
- Pass a `bslib::bs_theme()` to fill the character's primary and secondary brand roles (experimental role mapping).
- By default, `mode = "auto"` follows `bslib::input_dark_mode()` or Quarto's dark mode, and stays light when the page gives no signal.
- Not sure which colours to pick? Try them first in **Theme a mascot**: `mascot_studio(view = "theme")`.

```{r palettes-and-roles}
mascot_palettes("tessa")
```

```{r theme-examples, eval=FALSE}
pink_theme <- mascot_theme(
  light = list(body = "#B53D78", rim = "#A94A82"),
  dark = list(body = "#F2A6CF", rim = "#C5B0EB")
)

mascot("helper", theme = pink_theme)
update_mascot("helper", theme = "coral_navy")
```

## Motion

On a busy review dashboard where extra movement would distract people, you can quieten or stop animation while keeping every mood and message working.

- Pass `motion = FALSE` to [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) or [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) to stop all movement at once.
- Use [`mascot_motion_settings()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_motion_settings.html")`) to switch `idle`, `mood_change`, `gestures`, `swap`, `minimising`, `restoring` and `messages` on or off individually.
- Any switch left as `NULL` follows `others` (`TRUE` by default), so `others = FALSE` with `gestures = TRUE` allows only gestures.
- A user's browser or system reduced-motion preference always wins over `TRUE`.
- Idle breathing and blinking stop within five seconds of an action, and [`mascot_gesture()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_gesture.html")`) triggers one-off movements when allowed.

```{r motion-helpers, results="hide"}
mascot_motion_settings(idle = FALSE)
mascot_motion_settings(others = FALSE, gestures = TRUE)
```

```{r motion-app, eval=FALSE}
mascot("still_helper", motion = FALSE)
update_mascot("still_helper", motion = mascot_motion_settings(idle = FALSE))
```

## Clicks and menus

A mascot is a plain image by default so keyboard users never land on a dead control, but `click` turns it into a button or a menu.

- Leave `click = NULL` in [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) when clicking the character does nothing.
- Pass a label like `click = "Open help"` or [`mascot_action()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_action.html")`) for a single action that counts clicks in `input$<id>_click`.
- Pass [`mascot_popup_menu()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_popup_menu.html")`) with a named character vector to open a menu that sends the chosen item's name to `input$<id>_menu`.
- Opening or closing a menu never changes `input$<id>_click`, and dragging never counts as a click.
- Keyboard users can Tab to the button, press Enter or Space, use arrow keys in the menu, and press Escape to close it.
- Set `disabled = TRUE` to pause clicks during a slow task, or pass an empty helper to [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) to remove the click.

```{r clicks-and-menus, eval=FALSE}
mascot(
  "helper",
  click = mascot_popup_menu(c(finish = "Finish review", reset = "Reset helper"))
)

observeEvent(input$helper_menu, {
  if (identical(input$helper_menu, "finish")) {
    update_mascot(
      "helper",
      mood = "happy",
      status = "Review complete",
      bubble = mascot_bubble("All checks finished.", duration = Inf),
      gesture = mascot_gesture("nod")
    )
  }
})
```

## Shiny modules

When you split a larger Shiny app into modules, including `golem` and `rhino` apps, each module can own and update its own mascot.

- In the module UI, call [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) with a namespaced id such as `mascot(ns("helper"))`.
- Pass the plain local id `"helper"` to [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) inside `shiny::moduleServer()`.
- Read `input$helper_click`, `input$helper_menu`, `input$helper_position` and `input$helper_minimised` directly from that module's `input`.
- For one shared corner mascot across modules, return a reactive from each module and update the parent mascot from the top-level server.
- Run [`mascot_example()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_example.html")`) with `"modules"`, `"golem"` or `"rhino"` to see full working apps.

```{r shiny-module, eval=FALSE}
review_ui <- function(id) {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)
  shiny::tagList(
    shiny::actionButton(ns("finish"), "Finish review"),
    mascot(ns("helper"), placement = "inline")
  )
}

review_server <- function(id) {
  shiny::moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    shiny::observeEvent(input$finish, {
      update_mascot("helper", mood = "happy", status = "Review complete")
    })
  })
}
```

## Quarto pages

You can also place [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) in a rendered Quarto document with no Shiny server to show a fixed mood and status line.

- The character draws when the page loads, and stays static because there is no R session behind the page.
- Use `placement = "inline"` (or [`mascot_placement()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_placement.html")`)) to sit in the page flow, and give each mascot a unique `id`.
- On a static page that never shows a bubble, hide the reserved bubble space with `.mascot-bubble-region { display: none; }` in CSS.
- The mascot follows Quarto's light and dark theme toggle and works in self-contained pages (`embed-resources: true`).
- Quarto support is lightly tested so far, and a Quarto `shortcode` is planned for 0.2.0.

Put this in an R chunk of your `.qmd` file:

```r
#| echo: false
library(mascot)
mascot("helper", mood = "happy", status = "Rendered with Quarto", placement = "inline")
```

## Check a look before using it

Before wiring a character or colour theme into your app, you can inspect every mood and size on one offline page or try controls live in the studio.

- [`mascot_preview()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_preview.html")`) (experimental) builds a static offline page showing every mood in light and dark mode across your chosen size and 160, 96 and 24 pixels.
- Previews always draw mascots inline with `motion = FALSE` by default so you can compare faces side by side.
- Assign the result of `mascot_preview()` to inspect `attr(page, "contrast")` for any custom colours below 3:1 contrast, and print `page` to view it.
- [`mascot_studio()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_studio.html")`) (experimental) opens an offline app where you can test every function, check themes with `view = "theme"`, and copy R code.
- Use [`mascot_examples()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_examples.html")`) and [`mascot_example()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_example.html")`) to browse or open the seven bundled example apps.

```{r preview-and-studio, eval=FALSE}
page <- mascot_preview(
  theme = mascot_theme(
    light = list(body = "#B53D78", rim = "#A94A82"),
    dark = list(body = "#F2A6CF", rim = "#C5B0EB")
  )
)
attr(page, "contrast")

mascot_studio(view = "theme")
```

## Leave unchanged or reset

When you call [`update_mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-update_mascot.html")`) from the server, you can leave settings alone, replace them, or reset them to their defaults.

- Leaving an argument as `NULL` in `update_mascot()` keeps its current value, whereas `NULL` in [`mascot()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot.html")`) means none or the default.
- Passing an empty helper resets that setting to its starting state, as shown in the table below.
- Any non-`NULL` argument replaces that whole setting at once (for example, `size = 200` also resets `small_screen` to `"auto"`).
- If any value in `update_mascot()` is invalid, R warns and ignores the whole call so the mascot never updates halfway.
- Updates sent before a `shiny::renderUI()` mascot appears on screen are queued in order and applied as soon as it mounts.

| Setting | Reset sent to `update_mascot()` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Character | `character = `[`mascot_character()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_character.html")`) | Switches back to `"tessa"` |
| Mood | `mood = `[`mascot_mood()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_mood.html")`) | Returns to `"idle"` |
| Size | `size = `[`mascot_size()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_size.html")`) | Resets to `160` pixels (`small_screen = "auto"`) |
| Custom status | `status = `[`mascot_status()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_status.html")`) | Follows the mood again |
| Bubble | `bubble = `[`mascot_bubble()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_bubble.html")`) | Removes the speech bubble |
| Theme | `theme = `[`mascot_theme()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_theme.html")`) (or `"original"`) | Restores the character's own colours |
| Click | `click = `[`mascot_action()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_action.html")`) (or [`mascot_popup_menu()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_popup_menu.html")`)) | Makes the mascot a picture again |
| Placement | `placement = `[`mascot_placement()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_placement.html")`) | Floats in `"bottom-right"` (`"inline"` for inline) |
| Motion | `motion = `[`mascot_motion_settings()`](`r paste0(site_url, "articles/guide-mascot_motion_settings.html")`) | Allows movement again |

```{r reset-examples, eval=FALSE}
# Change only the mood; status, bubble and theme stay as they were:
update_mascot("helper", mood = "thinking")

# Reset custom status, clear the bubble, and restore original colours:
update_mascot(
  "helper",
  status = mascot_status(),
  bubble = mascot_bubble(),
  theme = mascot_theme()
)
```
